title: [AUG-112] Windows WASAPI loopback helper for direct system audio capture
why_we_need_this:
Follow-up to AUG-111. The Windows dshow path needs a loopback DirectShow device (Stereo Mix or VB-Cable). The dev PC — and most laptops with Bluetooth or USB headsets — has neither: Stereo Mix mirrors only the onboard Realtek output and modern Realtek UAD drivers often omit it. WASAPI loopback (AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_LOOPBACK on the default render endpoint) captures whatever the default output device is playing, Bluetooth included, with no virtual device and no "Listen to this device" trick. ffmpeg has no WASAPI input, so a small helper process is required. The user chose this over installing VB-Cable.

Design:
1. Helper source at @server/tools/wasapi-loopback/WasapiLoopback.cs — a single-file C# program using raw COM interop (IMMDeviceEnumerator, IAudioClient, IAudioCaptureClient), no NAudio or NuGet. Compiled on demand by the server with the .NET Framework compiler that ships with Windows 10/11 (C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\csc.exe) into config.dataDir/tools/wasapi-loopback.exe (gitignored); recompiled when the source hash changes. If csc.exe is missing the probe returns method 'none' with a hint.
2. Helper CLI: `wasapi-loopback.exe --probe` prints one JSON line to stdout {"sampleRate":48000,"channels":2,"format":"f32le","device":"<friendly name>"} and exits 0. `wasapi-loopback.exe` (no args) captures the default render endpoint in loopback mode and writes raw interleaved PCM in the mix format to stdout until stdin closes or the process is terminated; diagnostics go to stderr.
3. Silence fill: WASAPI loopback delivers no buffers while nothing is playing, which would shorten the file and break systemOffsetMs alignment. The helper tracks wall-clock frames since start and writes zero frames for any gap (AUDCLNT_BUFFERFLAGS_SILENT and missing packets) so stdout is a continuous real-time stream.
4. Server: new CaptureMethod 'wasapi-loopback' in @server/src/services/systemCapture.ts. probeWindowsMethod prefers wasapi-loopback (helper compiles and --probe succeeds), then falls back to dshow-loopback, then none. spawnCapturePipeline pipes helper stdout into ffmpeg (-f <format> -ar <rate> -ac <channels> -i pipe:0 → 16 kHz mono pcm_s16le, same flush/bitexact flags). Stop: terminate the helper (Node kill), ffmpeg sees EOF on pipe:0 and finalizes the WAV — the same EOF-based stop as coreaudio-tap; stopCaptureProcesses gets a 'wasapi-loopback' branch mirroring coreaudio-tap.
5. Self-test (AUG-106) and first-byte alignment (AUG-108) apply unchanged. Sidecar PIDs include the helper so orphan cleanup kills it.
6. captureCheck.ts prints the helper probe JSON and compile status on Windows. Hints: compile failure → excerpt of csc output; device missing → "No default output device".
7. Docs: architecture and preferences READMEs describe the helper, the compile-on-demand rule, the silence-fill invariant, and the method preference order.
acceptance_criteria:
- On this Windows PC (Bluetooth headphones as default output, no Stereo Mix, no VB-Cable), GET /api/capture/capabilities returns systemCapture true, method 'wasapi-loopback', the device name in the hint, and selfTest 'ok' while audio is playing or 'silent' when nothing plays.
- With System audio source = System or Auto, pressing Record produces a dual-track [Me]/[Them] session with no screen picker; the [Them] side transcribes audio played through the headphones.
- The helper compiles from source on first probe using csc.exe with no network access and no extra installs; the compiled exe lives under server/data/tools/ and is gitignored.
- Playing 5 s of audio, then 5 s of silence, then 5 s of audio during a capture yields a WAV of about 15 s, not about 10 s (silence fill works).
- POST /api/capture/stop returns a WAV with a valid header (ffprobe duration within 100 ms of the capture length).
- macOS behaviour and the dshow path are unchanged; when both WASAPI and a dshow loopback exist, WASAPI wins.
- Unit tests cover the probe JSON parser, the method preference order (fakes for helper/dshow availability), and the stopCaptureProcesses 'wasapi-loopback' sequence with a fake process.
- project-context/architecture and project-context/preferences READMEs document the helper.
important_constraints:
- No NuGet, no NAudio, no Node native addons; the only build tool is the csc.exe shipped with Windows.
- Keep the loopbackOnly guard on all capture endpoints; never expose the helper binary path to the client.
- Helper must never write anything but PCM to stdout.
